summary: The note argues that organizations and emergency services need a multi-layered communication strategy to stay connected during service disruptions such as blackouts, telecom failures and cyberattacks. It covers redundant channels, training and drills, resilient infrastructure with backup power, public-private coordination, new technology, and regulatory compliance with continuous improvement. It cites incidents from September 2023 to January 2024 and quotes Sandra M. Elliot and Mike Chen.
one_line: A guide to multi-layered emergency communication strategies for service disruptions, covering redundancy, drills, backup power, coordination, technology and compliance.
key_facts: A widespread blackout occurred on September 15, 2023, and a telecommunications failure hit several states on October 22, 2023.
Sandra M. Elliot is Director of Emergency Preparedness at the Telson Group; Mike Chen is Chief Technology Officer at Quantum Communications.
Primary communication channels are emails, phone calls and text messages, which need up-to-date contact lists but are not immune to outages.
On November 5, 2023, a cyberattack incapacitated local cellular networks, and emergency services in Redstone County used satellite communication and radio broadcasts to coordinate their response.
Mike Chen recommends mesh networks, which let devices communicate directly so information can reroute if one node goes down.
The earthquake alert in Coastal City on December 1, 2023, showed mass notification systems can effectively prompt evacuations and give safety instructions.
On January 3, 2024, a state-wide drill across Newbury State had all levels of emergency responders practice communication protocols under simulated widespread outages.
Sandra M. Elliot says regular testing and drills ensure equipment functions and keep personnel ready 'when every second counts.'
During the storm on September 30, 2023, backup generators were activated within minutes at the main communication relay center, preserving emergency response capabilities.
Data centers should have hardened physical and cyber security to prevent unauthorized access and attacks that cause outages.
Information-sharing protocols among utility companies, telecommunications providers and emergency services speed situational awareness and accurate public information.
Suggested technologies include advanced encryption, AI-driven response systems, and crowdsourcing social media and apps to reach diverse demographics.
Protocols should align with federal and state regulatory requirements, and after-action reviews feed continuous improvement.
